# Window: the round-9 closeout stamp v7.0.0 (9cb735dfc6, 2026-10-14T13:27:06Z) to the round-10 closeout stamp v10.0.0 (13cbe48de4, 2026-11-15T05:22:47Z), decision 0018 section 2 and decision 0016.

# Roster: dev/programme/rosters/wave-r10-groups.json at c080e93403e69543564ee334f0772229a28331b3 (the tip of handoff/audit-r10-roster when read, 548 groups). Product merges are read from main's first-parent history at 26dbf7c43e.

# MATCHING RULE, applied to every group of that roster. A group is a candidate when (1) it lists a file under custom_components/ or blueprints/, or its resume.pr is a first-parent merge of v7.0.0..26dbf7c43e that changed either directory, and (2) its source is outside, user or owner, or its kind is owner, bug, hotfix or defect, or its id holds HOTFIX or OUTSIDE, or its whitespace-normalised brief matches the regex in the second command. Every candidate has exactly one row below and every row is a candidate (98). Re-run from a checkout holding both commits:
#   git log --first-parent --merges --format='%H %s' v7.0.0..26dbf7c43e | while read h a b c n rest; do git diff --quiet $h^1 $h -- custom_components blueprints || echo "${n#\#}"; done > prod_prs.txt

#   git show c080e93403:dev/programme/rosters/wave-r10-groups.json | python3 -c "import json,sys,re; P=('custom_components/','blueprints/'); pp=set(open('prod_prs.txt').read().split()); R=re.compile(r\"owner[- ]report|outside report|owner-reported|reported by|report(ed)? on v\d|live user|live defect|live install|owner's install|owner's export|diagnostics (bundle|export|download)|issue #?\d{3,}|tvofi (reported|saw|found|asked)|in production|released (build|version)|on v\d+\.\d+\.\d+|\(tvofi,? 20\d\d-\d\d-\d\d|production defect\",re.I); [print(g['group']) for g in json.load(sys.stdin)['groups'] if (any(str(f).startswith(P) for f in g.get('files') or []) or str((g.get('resume') or {}).get('pr') or '') in pp) and (g.get('source') in ('outside','user','owner') or g.get('kind') in ('owner','bug','hotfix','defect') or 'HOTFIX' in g['group'] or 'OUTSIDE' in g['group'] or R.search(' '.join(str(g.get('brief')).split())))]"

# RULING, by hand from each candidate's brief: `in` = an objective bug (a judged finding of class bug, or an owner or outside report whose fix carries the failing-test-first proof fixer.md requires of every fix group) on a released version, reported inside the window by someone who is no finder seat of round 10; the owner's reports count (0018 section 5). `day0` = an owner report dated 2026-10-14, the stamp's own day, whose hour no tracked record holds: counted beside, never in `in`. `unreleased` = caused and caught inside the window before any release carried it: injected, no escape. `out` = no escape, the reason given: a finder's verified finding (found_by finder: removed), a report of a round-10 dimension's own seat (D15), a seat's report that is neither judged nor an outside report (seat), a feature, need or gap as the brief or its triage classes it, a duplicate of a rowed report, or a red on main that no release carried (programme).

# `owner` is the dimension whose perfect result (0018 section 1) the bug violates, `none` where no dimension brief owns it, `-` on an `out` row. `brief_sentence` is the brief's sentence that makes the row what it is, verbatim. `cause_pr` lists the merged pull requests that the brief, or the tracked root-cause record beside the group under dev/audit/rca/, names as the cause; space-separated. The R10 records under dev/audit/rca/ were searched for every `in` and `unreleased` group id; R10-RCA-COP-UNMEASURED.md and R10-RCA-COP-PARTLOAD.md name causes from before both windows (#50, v4.0.0; the v1.0.0 law), so they add none. Attribution is this record seat's; the evaluator re-reads it. Tab-separated.
